items.title: ‘Pharma Bro’ Martin Shkreli is in trouble with regulators again, this time for influencing biopharma stocks
items.description: The controversial investor has been weighing in on biopharma stocks even though he’s banned from doing so.

items.title: ‘I have no children’: My aunt gave me $50,000 for a down payment. Now she wants me to leave my home to her two children.
items.description: “The house cost $385,000. With my savings, her $50,000 and a small mortgage, I was able to close.”

items.title: ‘The house is worth $925,000’: My sister moved in with our mother, 78, and says she deserves the family home. Is she right?
items.description: “The house is worth $925,000 and mom owns it outright. She also has $480,000 in investments.”

items.title: ‘I am a pretty cautious person’: My financial adviser wants me to invest $350,000 in a UAE data center. Is this risky?
items.description: “I like my life, but I also like the idea of a big return after years of putting money into my 401(k).”

items.title: My wife says we can’t afford to retire, yet she wants to take an $8,000 trip to Italy. We have $4 million. Do I keep working?
items.description: “I worry about healthcare, long-term care, inflation, a long bear market and living to 95.”

items.title: Who should pay for a birthday dinner? I always treat my guests.
items.description: “I feel like I just end up paying for other people’s birthday dinners a lot, as well as my own, which is an imbalance.”

items.title: Hedge-fund legend Paul Tudor Jones says the stock market faces a really challenging 2027. Here’s why.
items.description: U.S. stocks could face a serious test in 2027 as a tsunami of new equity issuance threatens to upend the artificial-intelligence-driven bull market, according to hedge-fund billionaire Paul Tudor Jone

items.title: Six Flags’ stock slumps toward 16-year low after fatal incident
items.description: A fatal accident on a Six Flags Entertainment roller coaster sent shares of the amusement-park operator near the lowest level of the year.

items.title: Millions of Americans will have fewer options during Medicare open enrollment this year
items.description: There will be no Medicare Advantage plans in 181 counties in 2027, up from 67 in 2026.

items.title: UnitedHealth keeps medical costs under control — and raises its outlook again
items.description: The health-insurance giant said its medical-cost ratio was 88.4% in the third quarter of this year, as the company tries to rein in spending on medical care.
